title: Ambarisha Maharaja
subtitle: The Devotee Who Defeated a Sage

pages.text:
Long, long ago, in the golden kingdom of Mathura, there lived a great king named Ambarisha Maharaja. He was not just a powerful king — he was one of the greatest devotees of Lord Vishnu in the whole world.

Every single day, Ambarisha would wake up before sunrise, take a bath, and offer his prayers to Lord Vishnu with a pure and loving heart.

Ambarisha Maharaja had a rule in his kingdom: everyone would fast on the day called Ekadashi — a very special day dedicated to Lord Vishnu. And on the next day, called Dvadashi, they would break their fast together.

Ambarisha had been fasting for an entire year, and now it was time to break his fast. He had prepared a beautiful feast and was about to eat when suddenly...

A great sage named Durvasa arrived at the palace! Durvasa Muni was famous for two things: his incredible wisdom AND his very, very hot temper.

'O King,' said Durvasa, 'I would like to dine with you today!' Ambarisha was overjoyed and welcomed the sage with great respect. But Durvasa said he needed to take a bath in the river first and would return soon.

Ambarisha waited patiently. And waited. And waited some more. The precious minutes of Dvadashi were running out! His priests came to him worried: 'O King, if you don't break your fast right now, the auspicious time will pass!'

Ambarisha was in a difficult position. If he ate without the sage, it would seem rude. But if he didn't eat in time, he would break his vow to Lord Vishnu!

After careful thought, Ambarisha decided to drink just a tiny sip of water — enough to technically break his fast, but not enough to be a full meal without his guest.

Just then, Durvasa Muni came back. He saw what happened and his face turned red with anger! 'How DARE you eat without me!' he roared, his eyes blazing like fire.

Durvasa pulled a lock of his hair and created a powerful demon called Kritya from it! 'Go and destroy this disrespectful king!' he commanded.

But Ambarisha Maharaja stood calm and still, his mind peacefully resting on Lord Vishnu. He did not run. He did not fight back. He simply prayed.

Suddenly, a blazing wheel of light appeared — the Sudarshana Chakra of Lord Vishnu! It was Lord Vishnu's own weapon, which protects his pure devotees.

The Sudarshana Chakra burned the demon to ashes in an instant! Then it turned toward Durvasa Muni himself, chasing him all across the three worlds!

Durvasa ran everywhere — to Lord Brahma, to Lord Shiva, to the heavens — but no one could stop the Sudarshana Chakra. Finally, he went to Lord Vishnu himself.

'I am always with my devotees,' said Lord Vishnu. 'Go back to Ambarisha — only he can save you now.'

Durvasa returned, ashamed. When Ambarisha saw the sage suffering, his heart filled with compassion. With deep love and prayer, he asked the Sudarshana Chakra to stop — and it did.

The king and the sage shared a meal in peace. The end! 🙏

title: Dhruva Maharaja
subtitle: The Little Boy Who Became a Star

pages.text:
Once upon a time, there was a five-year-old prince named Dhruva. He lived in a great palace with his father, King Uttanapada.

One day, Dhruva saw his stepbrother sitting happily on their father's lap. Dhruva ran forward with a big smile, wanting to sit there too — but his stepmother stopped him coldly.

'You may not sit on the king's lap,' she said. Little Dhruva's eyes filled with tears.

Dhruva ran to his mother Suniti, crying. She hugged him and said softly: 'The only one who can truly give you what you deserve is Lord Vishnu himself. Go to the forest and pray to Him with all your heart.'

With a determined heart, the little five-year-old prince walked alone out of the palace — toward the deep, dark forest.

On his way, he met the wise sage Narada Muni, who taught him a special prayer and sent him to meditate at Madhuvana forest.

Dhruva sat under a tree and began to meditate. For one month, he ate only fallen leaves and fruits. For another month, he ate only water. He breathed very slowly and kept his mind only on Lord Vishnu.

His meditation became so powerful that all the world began to tremble! The gods in heaven were afraid.

'Something extraordinary is happening on Earth!' they said.

After five months of intense meditation, Lord Vishnu himself appeared before little Dhruva, riding on Garuda, glowing like a thousand suns!

Dhruva opened his eyes and was so overwhelmed he couldn't speak. Lord Vishnu gently touched his cheek with his conch shell — and immediately, beautiful words of prayer poured from Dhruva's heart.

Lord Vishnu smiled. 'Now that you have seen Me, do you still want a place on your father's lap?'

Dhruva thought deeply. He said, 'O Lord, I am ashamed that I came here seeking something so small. You are everything!'

Lord Vishnu smiled deeply. 'Dear Dhruva, your determination is truly remarkable. You shall have the Dhruva Loka — the Pole Star! You will shine there for millions of years, and all the stars in the sky will revolve around you.'

And when Dhruva's time came, a golden airplane from heaven took him up, up, up — to become the glowing Pole Star we see to this very day! 🌟 The end!

title: Prahlada and Narasimha
subtitle: The Boy Whose Love Could Not Be Stopped

pages.text:
Long ago, there was a powerful demon king named Hiranyakashipu. He had received a special boon — he could not be killed by any human, animal, god, or demon. He could not be killed inside or outside, during day or night, on the ground or in the sky.

With this power, he declared: 'I AM GOD. Worship only me!'

But Hiranyakashipu had a son named Prahlada — and Prahlada was completely different from his father.

Even as a tiny baby, Prahlada had heard stories of Lord Vishnu while inside his mother's womb. So from the very beginning, his heart was full of love for the Lord.

No matter what his father said, Prahlada would smile and say: 'Lord Vishnu is everywhere. He loves us all.'

Hiranyakashipu tried everything to stop Prahlada.

He threw him off a cliff — but Prahlada was caught by Lord Vishnu's invisible hands. He threw him into a fire — but the boy sat peacefully in the flames, chanting, and was not burned. He had wild elephants try to trample him — but the elephants gently nudged away.

Nothing could harm Prahlada, because the Lord was always with him.

'Where is your Vishnu now?!' shouted Hiranyakashipu. 'Is he in this pillar?!'

Prahlada smiled calmly. 'Yes, Father. Lord Vishnu is everywhere — even in that pillar.'

Hiranyakashipu struck the pillar with his fist.

CRACK! The pillar split open with a thunderous sound that shook the universe! From inside burst a form half-man, half-lion, with blazing eyes and a golden mane — Lord Narasimha!

Lord Narasimha placed Hiranyakashipu on his lap — neither on ground nor sky. At the doorway — neither inside nor outside. At twilight — neither day nor night. With his claws — neither weapon nor human hands. The boon was fulfilled!

Then little Prahlada walked forward quietly. With complete love, he placed his small hands in prayer.

Lord Narasimha's fierce expression melted into the most loving smile. He placed his hand on Prahlada's head.

'Your love for me has never wavered,' said the Lord. 'You are truly extraordinary.' 🙏 The end!

title: Rama and Sita
subtitle: The Prince Who Kept His Promise

pages.text:
In the beautiful kingdom of Ayodhya, there lived a prince named Rama. He was tall, strong, kind, and brave — the most beloved prince in all the land.

Everyone in the kingdom loved Rama dearly. He always kept his promises, always spoke the truth, and always protected those who needed help.

King Dasharatha, his father, had three queens and four sons — but Rama was the eldest and would one day become king.

In the kingdom of Mithila, King Janaka had a beautiful daughter named Sita — kind, wise, and full of grace.

King Janaka said: 'Whoever can lift and string the great bow of Lord Shiva shall win Sita's hand!'

Many mighty kings tried and failed — the bow was impossibly heavy. Then Rama stepped forward. He lifted the bow as easily as picking up a flower, strung it — and SNAP! The bow broke from its own power!

Rama and Sita were married with great joy. 💕

But just before Rama was to be crowned king, his stepmother Kaikeyi demanded that Rama be sent to the forest for fourteen years — and her own son Bharata become king instead.

Rama's heart did not break with anger. He simply said: 'Father gave his word. I will go.'

Sita refused to stay behind. 'Where you go, I go,' she said firmly. His brother Lakshmana also followed. And so the three walked into the deep forest together.

In the forest, the demon king Ravana of Lanka heard about Sita's beauty and goodness. He devised a cunning plan.

He lured Rama and Lakshmana away with a trick, and then — disguised as a holy man — he kidnapped Sita and carried her away in his flying chariot to the island of Lanka!

When Rama returned to find Sita gone, his heart was broken with grief. But he did not give up. He would find her — no matter what it took.

Rama and Lakshmana searched everywhere. Then they met Hanuman — the mighty devotee of Rama who could fly and move mountains!

Hanuman leapt across the great ocean to Lanka, found Sita kept prisoner in a garden, and gave her Rama's ring as a sign. 'Lord Rama is coming!' he promised her.

With a great army of brave monkeys, Rama built a bridge across the ocean to Lanka.

The great battle of Lanka began! Rama's army fought bravely. Arrow after arrow flew through the sky. After many days of fierce battle, Rama faced Ravana himself.

With his divine arrow — a gift from the gods — Rama defeated Ravana and rescued Sita!

The fourteen years were over. Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana returned home to Ayodhya. The whole kingdom burst into celebration with flowers, lights, and music.

The day they returned is celebrated even today as Diwali — the Festival of Lights! 🪔 The end!

title: Hanuman the Brave
subtitle: The Devotee Who Moved a Mountain

pages.text:
Long ago, there was a monkey named Hanuman. But he was no ordinary monkey!

Hanuman was the son of the wind god Vayu, which meant he could fly as fast as the wind itself. He was incredibly strong — strong enough to pick up a mountain! And he was the most devoted servant of Lord Rama that ever lived.

Whenever Hanuman chanted 'Jai Shri Ram!', his heart filled with so much energy that he felt he could do anything!

When Rama needed someone to cross the great ocean to find Sita in Lanka, everyone looked at each other nervously. The ocean was enormous — no one could cross it!

Then Hanuman closed his eyes, thought of Rama, and said: 'Jai Shri Ram!'

He grew larger and larger, took a mighty stance on the mountain, and LEAPT — soaring through the sky like a comet, across the entire ocean to Lanka in one single bound! 🌊

All the gods in heaven watched in wonder.

In Lanka, Hanuman searched everywhere. Finally, in a beautiful garden called Ashoka Vatika, he found Sita — sitting alone under a tree, sad but strong.

Hanuman showed her Rama's ring. Sita's eyes filled with tears of hope.

'Tell Rama I am waiting,' she said. 'Tell him I have not lost faith.'

Before leaving, Hanuman allowed himself to be captured by Ravana's soldiers — so he could deliver a bold message directly to the demon king!

Ravana was furious when he saw Hanuman. 'Set his tail on fire!' he ordered.

But Hanuman's tail kept growing longer and longer as they wrapped cloth and oil around it. Finally, they lit it — but Hanuman snapped his ropes, sprang free, and leapt from rooftop to rooftop across Lanka!

The fire from his tail set the demon city ablaze! Then he dipped his tail in the ocean, leapt back across the sea, and returned to Rama with the news. 🔥

In the great battle of Lanka, Lakshmana was struck by a powerful weapon and lay unconscious. The healers said only one herb — the Sanjeevani from the Himalayas — could save him. And it must arrive before sunrise!

Hanuman flew to the Himalayas. But in the dark, he couldn't find the exact herb. So Hanuman picked up the ENTIRE MOUNTAIN and carried it back!

Lakshmana was healed. The battle was won.

When Rama embraced Hanuman with love, Hanuman said: 'I need nothing else. Being in your service is my greatest treasure.' 💕 The end!

Long ago, two great armies stood on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, ready to fight.

On one side stood the Pandavas — five brave princes led by the mighty archer Arjuna. On the other side stood the Kauravas — a hundred cousins who had stolen the Pandavas' kingdom through cheating and cruelty.

Arjuna stood in his chariot, his bow in hand. His charioteer was his dearest friend — Lord Krishna himself, who had chosen to guide Arjuna rather than fight.

Arjuna looked across the battlefield. He saw his own grandfather Bhishma, his beloved teacher Drona, his cousins, uncles, and friends — all standing on the other side.

His hands began to shake. His bow slipped. Tears filled his eyes.

'Krishna,' he said, 'I cannot fight. These are my own family. How can I hurt the people I love? What is the point of a kingdom if everyone I love is dead?'

Arjuna sat down in his chariot, overwhelmed with grief and confusion.

Krishna looked at Arjuna with gentle eyes and said: 'Dear friend, why are you sad? The soul never dies. It just moves from one body to another — like changing clothes. So no one is truly destroyed.'

'But more importantly — you are a warrior. Your duty is to fight for what is right and true. Running away from your duty out of fear is not kindness — it is weakness.'

Arjuna listened carefully. These were words he had never heard before.

Krishna said: 'You have the right to do your work — but never cling to the results. Do your best, give everything, and leave the rest to God. This is the secret of a peaceful heart.'

'Whether you win or lose, whether people praise you or criticize you — stand firm in what is right. That is true strength.'

Arjuna felt something shift in his heart. The confusion was melting away. Courage was returning.

'Krishna,' said Arjuna, 'may I see your true form?'

Krishna smiled and gave Arjuna divine eyes. Arjuna saw a vision so magnificent, so enormous — with countless suns blazing, all of creation flowing in and out — that he trembled with awe.

'I am time itself,' said Krishna. 'I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all things. Know Me — and be fearless.'

Arjuna fell to his knees in wonder. 'Now I understand,' he said. 'I am ready.'

Arjuna picked up his bow with steady hands. His doubt was gone. His heart was clear.

The battle of Kurukshetra was fought, and the Pandavas won — but more than the battle, Arjuna had won something greater: wisdom.

The teachings that Krishna gave Arjuna that day were written down as the Bhagavad Gita — the Song of God. People have read these words for thousands of years.

They teach us: Do what is right. Work hard without worrying about results. Love God. Be kind. Be brave.

These lessons are as true today as they were on that ancient battlefield. 🙏 The end!

King Bharat was one of the greatest kings who ever lived. He ruled the whole world wisely and with great love. In fact, our country India is named 'Bharata' after him!

After many years of ruling, Bharat gave up his kingdom to go to the forest, meditate, and think only about God. He went to a beautiful place called Shalagrama and began his peaceful life of prayer.

One day, sitting by the river, Bharat saw a pregnant deer startled by a lion. She gave birth right there — and the tiny fawn fell into the river!

Bharat's heart was flooded with compassion. He waded in and saved the little deer.

He brought the fawn home and began to care for it every single day. Slowly, slowly, Bharat began spending more time with the deer... and less time in meditation.

His mind, which once rested on God, was now always thinking about the little deer.

When Bharat's time came, his last thought was of his beloved deer — and so he was reborn as a deer himself!

But even as a deer, Bharat remembered his past life. 'I let attachment distract me,' he thought. This time, he lived quietly, alone, remembering God.

When the deer-body ended, Bharat was born again as a human — this time in a family of wise teachers.

This new Bharat appeared very strange to everyone. He would not speak. He would just sit quietly, doing whatever work was given to him — whether praised or insulted, whether hot or cold. Nothing disturbed his inner peace.

His brothers thought he was simple and called him 'Jada Bharata' — the unmoving Bharat.

But inside, he was completely free. His mind rested only on God. He had learned the lesson of his deer life: never let attachment take you away from what truly matters.

What looks like silence is sometimes the deepest wisdom. 🙏 The end!
